content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To catch a butterfly for a pet, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase a specialized butterfly mesh net (20 minutes)
Step 2. Research the specific migration patterns of local species (3 hours)
Step 3. Assemble a large mesh pop-up enclosure (15 minutes)
Step 4. Buy a botanical guide to local wildflowers (10 minutes)
Step 5. Scout a sunny location in the backyard for the release (1 hour)
Step 6. Purchase high-quality sugar and sponges for feeding (30 minutes)
Step 7. Clear a space in the garage for supply storage (2 hours)
Step 8. Plant a variety of nectar-rich flowers like Zinnias (4 hours)
Step 9. Visit a local lepidopterist for expert advice (2 hours)
Step 10. Install a small outdoor water mister (45 minutes)
Step 11. Prepare a sugar-water solution for the feeding station (15 minutes)
Step 12. Set up a magnifying station for observation (30 minutes)
Step 13. Drive to a local nursery to select host plants (1 hour)
Step 14. Place fresh fruit slices on a feeding tray (10 minutes)
Step 15. Catch a healthy butterfly in the garden (45 minutes)
Step 16. Order a butterfly field identification kit online (15 minutes)
Step 17. Clean the feeding trays with organic soap (20 minutes)
Step 18. Buy a soft-bristled brush for gentle handling (5 minutes)
Step 19. Hang the sponges soaked in nectar (20 minutes)
Step 20. Install a thermometer inside the enclosure (10 minutes)
Step 21. Buy a sturdy outdoor table for the enclosure (1 hour)
Step 22. Level the ground where the mister will be placed (30 minutes)
Step 23. Research which host plants attract specific caterpillars (2 hours)
Step 24. Place the table in a wind-protected area (15 minutes)
Step 25. Place the butterfly carefully into the enclosure (5 minutes)
Step 26. Transplant the host plants into large pots (2 hours)
Step 27. Apply organic fertilizer to the potted plants (15 minutes)
Step 28. Wait for the nectar flowers to bloom (2 weeks)
Step 29. Check the weather forecast for a sunny day (5 minutes)
Step 30. Drive to the hardware store for supplies (40 minutes)
Step 31. Read a book on butterfly anatomy (4 hours)
Step 32. Buy a bag of high-quality potting soil (20 minutes)
Step 33. Buy a garden hose and spray nozzle (25 minutes)
Step 34. Mix the soil with organic compost (1 hour)
Step 35. Buy a set of small glass jars for temporary holding (20 minutes)
Step 36. Search for local butterfly enthusiast clubs (30 minutes)
Step 37. Take a quiz on butterfly species identification (30 minutes)
Step 38. Buy a decorative butterfly puddling stone (40 minutes)
Step 39. Label the different plant species (30 minutes)
Step 40. Download a butterfly tracking mobile app (5 minutes)
